authority.note: The sealed hallway architecture gives Earth the elevated climb above the performers and the overlook signature move; the Phase 0 canon row gives the verb COMPARE, the barrier ELEVATION and the payoff of three unison figures aligned. The 2026-09-08 regrade keeps the climb as a dead-end spur and adds a working catwalk 1.4 m above the row, because the terraced room failed its own sightline criterion at every case. Tracker question LweZ97oG (Earth Compression) is unanswered and nothing here depends on it.

claims.statement: The three cases are the TOGETHER-SAME row: G pro/pro, H anti/anti, I blue anti with red pro, bound to the live catalog ids tnd-tog-same-gggg, -hhhh and -iiii.

Out of the vestibule one ramp climbs 1.8 m to a dead-end overlook spur and another falls 1.0 m to a catwalk that runs the row 1.4 m above the rootbed. There is no way down onto the bed. The terrain is 2.5D, so the spur is walked and walked back rather than looped.

The payoff is a single eye on the landing at plan (30.5, 13.0), from which the three unison figures nest away down one axis and read as one shape at three scales: 3.79 m at 22.5 degrees, 10.60 m at 7.9, 17.56 m at 4.7.
Elemental associations are never spoken in the wing. The only text on the shell is the class stamp TOGETHER-SAME and the three case letters.

Three control consoles are set into the catwalk south rail, one opposite each case, capped level with the door datum. From a console its own case reads at 4.28 m and 22.7 degrees below the horizon with the foot line clear, which is the acceptance criterion of at most 6.00 m and 25 degrees. The consoles are geometry in the plan contract; no interaction reads or writes a sequence through them yet.

evidence.note: Carves the REGRADED room: vestibule at the door datum, the entry ramp climbing east to the +1.8 overlook spur, the descent ramp west of the gallery, and the catwalk causeway at -1.0 with its three alcoves. Four rail runs (52 posts), three rail consoles with their cut-stone letters, 14 lanterns and 14 roots. Every deck-mounted foot starts FOOT_SINK 0.55 below its deck so the production floor sink and the voxel edge rounding cannot leave it in mid-air. Adds two QA-only cameras, console-stance and catwalk-run, which never enter the manifest.

Written by the regraded build and carries sourceDigest f756a2b1, which is the manifest the contract stamps. 131 exported meshes, 8 materials, 52 rail posts, footSink 0.55, the three consoles at deck -1.0 with caps at 0.0, and the split camera lists: eight contract cameras, two QA-only.

checks.name: shell-continuity
checks.evidence: The carve takes 18 route operands into one ET_Shell_Rock, 998 faces cleaned to 997 with no orphan (graybox report). The production pass then builds the void from the same carve at 1035 faces and closes it into a single 67536-triangle shell after removing 3878 outside caps, which a discontinuous route would not do. The ramp-climb, catwalk-run and ensemble renders show unbroken rock at every deck seam and under the causeway.

checks.name: collision-parity
checks.evidence: The graybox is authored from the hash-stamped manifest (sourceDigest f756a2b1) that the runtime terrain program is exported from, so the decks land on the plan datums by construction. What the pipeline then does to them was measured rather than assumed: ray-probing the production blend across the catwalk band (x -4/0/3/6/10 by y 2.2 to 5.4) reads the deck at -1.12 to -1.18 in its interior and -1.40 at the lip, against a -1.00 datum, and the bed at -2.5 against -2.40. That is FLOOR_SINK 0.12 plus the 0.30 m voxel rounding a deck edge down. Every measurement sits BELOW the collider and none above it, which is the invariant the sink exists for: the visitor never stands in rock. FOOT_SINK 0.55 in the graybox is what keeps the rail posts, console legs and lamp stems buried in that gap rather than floating over it.

evidence.note: Headless production build: remesh and skin the carved void, mound the rootbed through its own vertex group, split the rock into route and pit by the grown bed box, bake six lightmaps, render the QA views and optimise to WebP plus Draco. This pass adds the console export families - panel, cap and both legs to ET_Brass, the letter to ET_CutStone, the lit face beside the lantern heads - and an orphan guard that raises when any ET_ mesh is claimed by no family, because the first regrade pass would otherwise have shipped a room whose rail carried no consoles at all. Also lights the exit bore from inside and renders ten views.

The regraded room. 6075592 bytes. Two lightmapped rock pieces at 4096 (pit 37610 tris, route 29926) and four trim pieces at 1024 (brass 6520, stone 17792, root 3360, moss 4608), eight materials, 24 exported objects including the three console faces. 59.1 MB raw to 6.1 MB shipped.
Written by the build: source digest, per-piece triangle counts and lightmap sizes, texture sets, UV metres per unit, export and optimise settings.

Mounts the GLB at the room's plan centre, tunes the two emissive-only materials by name, ray-casts the mounded bed in the shell's own frame, stands four pedestals and four performers, registers four pooled point lights, dev seam window.__earth.
Seventeen numbered decisions, the verification pass, and what is left open.

Recorded in the 2026-09-07 decision record and summarised in the regrade spec; the raw evidence is session transcript be270ac6, which lives outside the repository. Full /museum grid on a task-owned worktree server, stopping at the Fire seam (90.5, 58.0), the corridor, the west door, the vestibule, the ramp, the terrace overlook, the landing ensemble eye and the exit approach, reading window.__earth at each. Zero console errors. The walk found and fixed two defects no test or QA render could show: the bed ray was cast in the wrong frame and never reached the shell, and the pedestal body was still the Drowned Gallery slate. It walked the pre-regrade room.

checks.name: runtime-console
checks.evidence: Walked in a task-owned browser on 2026-09-09 against a task-owned Vite on port 5437 (stopped in the same turn). /museum?room=cave-earth loads the regraded GLB - the served file is 6075592 bytes, not the 5717544-byte pre-regrade one - with zero console errors; the only entries are Vite reconnect noise and a PostHog no-API-key warning. window.__earth reads the player at (2.5, 0.85, 13.5) in the isolated frame, which is plan (1.25, 12.25) and Blender (-15.75, 0) against a contract spawn of (-15.8, 0) - the half-tile snap. Cases G, H and I are all active with topY -2.228, -2.227 and -2.284, and the four light slots read 34, 9, 9 and 14. The spawn view is the vestibule: the opener disc and its performer ahead, the entry ramp and its brass rail climbing away on the left, the wing stamp on the rock beyond. That is the read the regrade exists for, and it replaces the pre-regrade walk, which put the visitor face-first into a rock wall. One thing this walk did NOT establish: the player would not move. The docent auto-walk held KeyD for over a minute with the tile counter frozen at (5, 27). The identical stall reproduces in ?room=cave-fire, a room this work never touched, so it is not a Root Terrace defect - but locomotion under the isolated-room route is unproven here and wants its own pass.

checks.name: performance
checks.evidence: window.__earth.lights reads four declared slots at intensities 34, 9, 9 and 14. The pool hands the shader the nearest three and the visible-light count never changes, which is what keeps the three.js relink storm off this room. The regrade keeps the pool at exactly four.

checks.name: qa-renders
checks.evidence: Ten Cycles views of the regraded room in blender/qa/earth-root-terrace-production/ (not committed; blender/ is gitignored): threshold, ramp-climb, overlook, catwalk-run, console, console-stance, ensemble, exit, overview, plan. Eight register to contract cameras; catwalk-run and console-stance are QA-only. Two things to read them by. Every emissive is exaggerated for these frames (BAKE_EMISSION puts ET Sky at 42x and ET Lamp at 24x) so the lightmaps show as they were baked, which makes lanterns and console faces render as blown-white slabs; at export they ship at unity and the runtime tunes them by name. And overview and plan are shot from outside the shell, which the rock hides, so they read as rail diagrams rather than room views - that predates the regrade.

validatorState.explanation: One structural fact, reported six times, and it is unchanged by this rebuild. The validator derives currentGate as the index of the first gate that is not complete, and forbids any gate past currentGate from holding evidence or checks. No gate on this scene has ever been approved, so currentGate is 0, and every piece of real evidence gathered for gates 1, 2 and 4 is therefore illegal. There is no value of currentGate that both tells the truth and lets the evidence stand. The honest resolution is Austen approving gates as he reviews them, at which point currentGate rises legitimately and these errors disappear on their own. Do not resolve this by stamping approvals.
